problems.title: Compactness and continuity do not prove the stated pure-strategy equilibrium
problems.source_location: Section 2.5, Assumptions 1–2 and Theorem 1, Eq. (8), PDF p. 5; Appendix A, PDF pp. 13–14.
claim: Paraphrase: Assumption \(1\) and Assumption \(2\) in Section 2.5, p. 5, require a compact finite-dimensional joint strategy space and continuity in each player’s own strategy. Theorem 1, Eq. (8), concludes that a deterministic strategy tuple exists satisfying all unilateral best-response inequalities. Appendix A, pp. 13–14, strengthens the discussion to joint continuity and invokes Glicksberg as if compactness plus continuity guaranteed a pure-strategy Nash equilibrium. The same appendix then presents zero-gradient conditions for teacher and students in Eqs. (27), (\(28\)), and (\(32\)), pp. 14–15.

The student minimizes \(R_S=\lambda_u L_{\rm unsup}+\lambda_{\rm adv}L_{\rm adv}\); the generator maximizes expected entropy; the teacher’s simultaneous-game payoff is validation accuracy of the fixed students. Appendix A uses teacher constraints \(0\leq\tau,\lambda_u,\lambda_{\rm adv}\leq1\), \(\lambda_u+\lambda_{\rm adv}\leq1\), a bounded student parameter ball, and an \(\ell_\infty\) perturbation ball.
analysis: Compactness and continuity alone do not imply a pure-strategy equilibrium. For example, on \(x,y\in[-1,1]\), let player one maximize \((x-y)^2\) and player two minimize it. The second player's best response is \(y=x\), where the first can always improve by changing \(x\); no pure equilibrium exists. This disproves the generic inference, not the paper's full game. Its allowed zero loss weights yield a separate degenerate equilibrium with uniform students, so asserting nonexistence for that complete domain would be wrong.
result: The general compact-continuous-game proof is insufficient, but the paper's full zero-weight domain permits a degenerate equilibrium. This does not establish a false existence conclusion for that full game, so Minor is appropriate.
repair: Use a mixed-strategy statement for the generic compact continuous game, or supply a proof using the actual payoff structure. Preserve the direct zero-weight equilibrium as bare existence; replace boundary zero-gradient assertions with constrained optimality conditions and treat convergence separately.
problems.impact_rationale: The general compact-continuous-game proof is insufficient, but the paper's full zero-weight domain permits a degenerate equilibrium. This does not establish a false existence conclusion for that full game, so Minor is appropriate.

problems.title: The public teacher update scales a training gradient instead of differentiating validation performance
problems.source_location: Section 2.3, Eqs. (5)–(7), PDF p. 4; Algorithm 1, line 16, PDF p. 5; Appendix B, PDF pp. 15–16.
claim: Paraphrase: Section 2.3, p. 4, Eqs. (5)–(7), and Algorithm 1, p. 5, line 16, update teacher parameters according to the validation effect of the student update. Appendix B, pp. 15–16, describes a one-step unroll and validation differentiation through the inner gradient, while also using a first-order/Reptile description. Section 3, p. 6, says the initial threshold and weights are \((0.05,0.5,0.5)\) and are adaptively learned.
analysis: Let the inner loss be \(\lambda(w-1)^2/2\), \(\lambda=\operatorname{sigmoid}(\phi)\), start \(w=0\), and use step \(\eta=0.1\). The one-step student is \(w'=0.1\lambda\). For validation loss \((w'-1)^2/2\), differentiation at \(\phi=0\) gives \(-0.02375\). Scaling a direct training derivative does not compute that mixed derivative, and a Boolean threshold supplies no ordinary gradient. This distinguishes the released heuristic from the stated unrolled validation objective.

The current helper multiplies the direct training derivative \(0.125\) by detached validation loss \(0.45125\), giving \(0.05640625>0\), opposite to the one-step validation derivative \(-0.02375\). The threshold enters only a Boolean comparison and receives no ordinary derivative.
result: The current scalar-rescaled training gradient can oppose the specified validation meta-gradient and cannot adapt the hard threshold by ordinary differentiation; benchmark exposure is unresolved.
repair: Use an explicitly differentiable inner update when computing the outer validation derivative, or describe and evaluate the implemented heuristic as a different update. No restored benchmark performance is claimed.
problems.impact_rationale: The current scalar-rescaled training gradient can oppose the specified validation meta-gradient and cannot adapt the hard threshold by ordinary differentiation; benchmark exposure is unresolved.

problems.title: The public cross-view targets differ from the stated ensemble pseudo-labels
problems.source_location: Eqs. (1)–(2), PDF p. 3; Algorithm 1, lines 6–8, PDF p. 5.
claim: Paraphrase: Eq. (1), p. 3, defines MI from the ensemble predictive mean. The text accepts samples when \(I>\tau\), and the definition following Eq. (2) uses \(\hat y^{(i)}=\arg\max_y\bar p^{(i)}(y)\). Each student’s accepted pseudo-label is sent to the other student. Algorithm 1, p. 5, lines 6–8 repeats MI selection and cross-view supervision.
analysis: Dropout predictions \[(0.9,0.1),(0.1,0.9),(0.1,0.9)\] have ensemble argmax class \(1\), while the first draw selects class \(0\). A first-draw target is therefore not the stated ensemble target. Sender-based acceptance and an intersection of both students' acceptance masks are also distinct policies; the source must identify which it implements.
result: Current first-draw targets disagree with the explicitly defined ensemble, and acceptance-mask provenance is a separate policy choice; actual benchmark target errors are not measured.
repair: Compute the mean predictive probability vector before selecting its label, and specify whether acceptance uses the sending student or both students. Reversing an uncertainty inequality alone is not established as an accuracy repair.
problems.impact_rationale: Current first-draw targets disagree with the explicitly defined ensemble, and acceptance-mask provenance is a separate policy choice; actual benchmark target errors are not measured.

problems.title: Detaching MI removes its entire contribution to the generator gradient
problems.source_location: Section 2.2, Eq. (3), PDF p. 4; Algorithm 1, line 9, PDF p. 5.
claim: Section 2.2, Eq. (3), PDF p. 4, and the generator docstring use entropy plus a weighted mutual-information term. Algorithm 1, line 9, instead shows entropy alone, which is retained as counterevidence. Released methods/trico/generator.py, lines 11–17, differentiates its perturbed input, but utils.py, line 15, detaches the MI value, so that path has \(\nabla_x I=0\).
analysis: Detaching the computed mutual information makes its gradient with respect to generator parameters zero. It may remain a reported scalar or selection statistic, but cannot contribute the claimed differentiable MI pressure to that generator objective through the detached path.

With binary dropout logits \((x,0)\) and \((-x,0)\), let \(h(x)\) be their single-draw entropy. Their mean is uniform and \(I=\log2-h\). At \(x=1\), the intended \(h+2I\) derivative is \(+0.1966119332\), but detaching \(I\) leaves derivative \(-0.1966119332\). Sign perturbations of size \(0.1\) therefore go to \(1.1\) and \(0.9\), respectively.
result: The current detach removes the entire MI gradient and can reverse the stated joint-objective perturbation, while preserving the entropy-only variant and perturbation bound.
repair: Provide differentiable MI for the generator while detaching a separate selection statistic, or explicitly adopt and evaluate the entropy-only algorithmic variant.
problems.impact_rationale: The current detach removes the entire MI gradient and can reverse the stated joint-objective perturbation, while preserving the entropy-only variant and perturbation bound.

problems.title: The public launcher feeds the official test split into teacher updates
problems.source_location: Section 3, PDF p. 6 (validation/testing protocol); released launcher.
claim: Paraphrase: Section 3, p. 6, describes a fixed validation subset consisting of \(10\%\) of labeled training data for teacher feedback, with the official test set used for testing. This separation matters even if the teacher update is the heuristic identified in Problem 2, because the feedback still changes parameters used in later student learning.
analysis: Passing the official test split as validation data into the teacher's update objective uses held-out labels for training. In this launcher path the resulting score is not independent final testing. It does not establish that every historical paper run used the public launcher unchanged.
result: The actual launcher routes official test labels into adaptive teacher feedback; unchanged private experiment provenance and numerical score effects remain unknown.
repair: Construct an explicit stratified validation subset from the available labeled training examples before building the loaders. Keep its labels out of inner supervised training, preserve the declared label budget, and pass only this validation loader to teacher updates. Keep the official test loader solely in evaluation. Save split indices and seeds so disjointness and label counts can be checked independently. Runs produced by the defective path need retraining and fresh evaluation; reports from an independently correct private path would instead require provenance showing that separation. No numerical adjustment to existing accuracies can repair an adaptive test-label dependency.
problems.impact_rationale: The actual launcher routes official test labels into adaptive teacher feedback; unchanged private experiment provenance and numerical score effects remain unknown.

problems.title: The MI inequality needs a reliability-versus-uncertainty interpretation
problems.source_location: Eq. (1) and pseudo-acceptance discussion, PDF p. 3.
claim: The source uses a dropout mutual-information threshold in selecting pseudo-labels.
analysis: High epistemic disagreement does not itself guarantee a reliable label. It can be an intentional uncertainty curriculum, but that is a different rationale from confidence filtering; reversing the inequality alone has not been validated as an accuracy repair.
result: Scope clarification preserving uncertainty-based selection as a possible intentional policy.
assumptions: Bounded to the stated source/component; no published-run provenance inferred.
problems.impact_rationale: The authors' stated scope or counterevidence resolves the apparent contradiction; this is not counted as a supported paper error.

impact_rationale: The latest paper retains an insufficient generic equilibrium proof, with bare full-game existence separately recoverable. Current code retains local teacher/target/gradient and evaluation-contract discrepancies, without a benchmark-level refutation.
